items.title: A quantum probabilistic approach to the emergence of an inflationary Starobinsky Universe
items.topic: Minisuperspace · canonical quantisation · operator ordering · Hilbert-space measure
items.summary: Die am 14. Oktober 2026 auf arXiv eingestellte Dissertation untersucht die kanonische Quantisierung eines eindimensionalen Minisuperspace-Modells und Ordnungsmehrdeutigkeiten in der Wheeler-DeWitt-Gleichung. Aus der Hermitizität des Hamiltonoperators leitet sie Einschränkungen für die Ordnungsfunktionen und das Maß des Hilbertraum-Skalarprodukts ab. Über eine Umdefinition der Wellenfunktion und den Pfadintegralformalismus diskutiert sie eine ordnungsunabhängige Formulierung; anschließend behandelt sie die Verallgemeinerung auf mehrdimensionale Minisuperspace-Modelle und Wahrscheinlichkeitsamplituden im Starobinsky-Modell.
items.relevance: Konkreter methodischer Bezug zur kanonischen SER/SSS-Quantisierung von Koch und Riahinia: Hilbertraummaß, Selbstadjungiertheit und Ordnungswahl können die Berechnung geometrischer Erwartungswerte beeinflussen, die anschließend in die q-Desic-Gleichung eingehen. Eigene Anschlussfragen: Lässt sich das hier benutzte Kriterium der Ordnungsunabhängigkeit auf die SER-Hamilton- und Zusammenhangsoperatoren übertragen? Bleiben Erwartungswerte von inversen Metrikoperatoren und höheren Momenten unter solchen Umdefinitionen invariant? Die Arbeit selbst behandelt weder sphärisch-symmetrische Raumzeitoperatoren noch q-Desics.
items.notes: Neu auf arXiv am 14.10.2026; Dissertation bereits im Januar 2026 verteidigt. Teile der Methodik beruhen auf bereits publizierten Arbeiten von 2024/2025 (arXiv:2407.03077, 2412.18532, 2512.23656). Kein Anspruch, dass alle Resultate originär neu sind.

items.title: Linear Response to Black Hole Deformations
items.topic: Static spherical geometry · linear response · ISCO · black-hole shadows · q-desic observables
items.summary: The author develops a linear-response-inspired framework to calculate leading changes in observables when the Schwarzschild geometry is deformed. The size of the deformation is organised using an eigenvalue of the Einstein tensor, interpreted as an effective external energy-momentum source. The framework is applied to static, spherically symmetric black holes, including shifts in particle-orbit observables, shadow size and scalar quasinormal modes.
items.relevance: Direct methodological benchmark for q-desics: once SER quantisation supplies expectation values of metric and connection operators, the induced corrections to the photon sphere, ISCO or shadow could be compared with the metric-deformation response formalism. A crucial original question is whether corrections driven by <Gamma-hat> minus Gamma(<g-hat>) can be represented within the paper's metric-only parametrisation, or produce observational effects that cannot. This comparison is proposed here; it is not a result claimed by the author.
items.notes: New arXiv submission 13 October 2026; independently checked against the official abstract. This paper does not calculate quantum-geometric operator expectation values.

items.title: An exact rotating black hole solution in Palatini Kalb–Ramond gravity
items.topic: Metric-affine gravity · rotating black holes · q-desics benchmarks
items.summary: Constructs an exact stationary, axisymmetric vacuum solution by varying the metric, connection and Kalb–Ramond field independently. A Kerr auxiliary geometry determines the physical metric. The paper derives timelike and null trajectories, circular-orbit stability and perihelion advance, and computes photon critical curves; the Kerr limit is recovered when the deformation parameter vanishes.
items.relevance: A methodological comparison for q-desics: it treats metric and connection as independent geometric variables and connects a rotating geometry to orbital and photon observables. This relevance assessment is an inference; the model is classical metric-affine gravity, rather than a calculation of quantum expectation values or SER quantisation.
items.notes: Reported in the morning digest on 12 October 2026; arXiv submission: 9 October 2026. The only paper recovered from that morning’s report.

items.title: Analytic solutions for the gravitational spin Hall equations and black hole shadows
items.topic: Beyond-geodesic propagation · photon trajectories · black hole shadows
items.summary: Derives analytic solutions of the gravitational spin Hall equations to first order in wavelength for a broad class of type D black-hole spacetimes with analytically solvable null geodesics. The framework also gives polarization-dependent corrections to black-hole shadow shapes.
items.relevance: An inferred comparison benchmark for q-desic photon propagation and shadow observables: it provides controlled departures from null-geodesic motion. Its corrections arise from finite-wavelength and polarization effects in classical wave propagation, rather than quantum spacetime expectation values.
items.notes: Reported in the morning digest on 11 October 2026. Date shown is the arXiv submission date. Relevance rating retained from that report.

items.title: Horizon-Scale Corrections to Black Hole Geometry from a Conserved Quantum Atmosphere
items.topic: Semiclassical geometry · horizon shifts · orbital observables
items.summary: Models a coarse-grained near-horizon atmosphere as a conserved anisotropic source and solves for a static black-hole geometry at fixed ADM mass. The resulting mean geometry changes the horizon and surface gravity together with timelike effective potentials, ISCO location and near-horizon residence times. Stochastic metric fluctuations are left for a subsequent treatment.
items.relevance: An inferred benchmark for linking quantum-inspired geometric changes to orbital observables. It helps distinguish motion in a dressed mean metric from q-desics governed by the expectation value of a connection, which need not equal the connection of the mean metric.
items.notes: Reported in the morning digest on 11 October 2026. Date shown is the arXiv submission date. Relevance rating retained from that report.

items.title: Pre-geometric Black Holes with Spherical Symmetry
items.topic: Spherical geometry · pre-geometric gravity · SER comparisons
items.summary: Constructs exact spherically symmetric vacuum configurations in pre-geometric theories using a correspondence principle. The solutions are analogues of Schwarzschild–(anti-)de Sitter geometries; one has a Planck-scale (anti-)de Sitter core. The paper also examines a pre-geometric version of Birkhoff’s theorem.
items.relevance: An inferred conceptual comparison for SER quantisation: both investigate spherical spacetime beyond the usual classical description. This paper concerns pre-geometric solutions and emergent metrics; it does not itself compute the metric or connection operator expectation values needed for q-desics.
